- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to compensate.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at +3–5% above peak for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive mid-horizon, model often fails to adjust; re-estimate from midpoint of sentiment transition.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 5-day average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overfit recent volatility; smooth with 3–5 day moving average of true values before forecasting.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “0.33” or “0.67” alternation, model often misreads trend; use sentiment-weighted average of last 3–5 days for correction.
